From 6ccbb613b42a1f1ba7bfd547a148f644a902a25c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 17:23:39 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] arm_mpam: Check whether the config array is allocated before
 destroying it

__destroy_component_cfg() is called to free the configuration array.
It uses the embedded 'garbage' structure, which means the array has
to be allocated.

If __destroy_component_cfg() is called from mpam_disable() before the
configuration was ever allocated, then a NULL pointer is dereferenced.

Check for this case and return early if the configuration is not
allocated.

__destroy_component_cfg() also frees the mbwu_state as this is allocated
by __allocate_component_cfg(). As the mbwu_state is allocated after
comp->cfg is set, and is also under mpam_list_lock, only the first
pointer needs checking.

Fixes: 3bd04fe7d807 ("arm_mpam: Extend reset logic to allow devices to be reset any time")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Ben Horgan <ben.horgan@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c b/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
index 5c48812d8573..988fc291241d 100644
--- a/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
+++ b/drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c
@@ -2581,6 +2581,9 @@ static void __destroy_component_cfg(struct mpam_component *comp)
 
 	lockdep_assert_held(&mpam_list_lock);
 
+	if (!comp->cfg)
+		return;
+
 	add_to_garbage(comp->cfg);
 	list_for_each_entry(vmsc, &comp->vmsc, comp_list) {
 		msc = vmsc->msc;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

### Modifications per file

**`drivers/resctrl/mpam_devices.c`**  
- In the function `__destroy_component_cfg()`, an early return was added:  
  If `comp->cfg` is `NULL`, the function returns immediately without proceeding to the destruction logic.

### Relationships between modifications

The change is confined to a single function within one file. The added guard condition (`if (!comp->cfg) return;`) prevents a NULL pointer dereference that would occur when `__destroy_component_cfg()` is called from `mpam_disable()` before the configuration array (`comp->cfg`) has ever been allocated. Since `comp->cfg` is the first pointer set during configuration allocation (and `mbwu_state` is allocated later under the same lock), checking only `comp->cfg` is sufficient to determine whether any destruction is needed. This preserves the existing behavior for normal cases while avoiding a crash in the early-disable scenario.

arm_mpam: Check whether the config array is allocated before
 destroying it

__destroy_component_cfg() is called to free the configuration array.
It uses the embedded 'garbage' structure, which means the array has
to be allocated.

If __destroy_component_cfg() is called from mpam_disable() before the
configuration was ever allocated, then a NULL pointer is dereferenced.

Check for this case and return early if the configuration is not

__destroy_component_cfg() also frees the mbwu_state as this is allocated
by __allocate_component_cfg(). As the mbwu_state is allocated after
comp->cfg is set, and is also under mpam_list_lock, only the first
pointer needs checking.

Fixes: 3bd04fe7d807 ("arm_mpam: Extend reset logic to allow devices to be reset any time")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: James Morse <james.morse@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Ben Horgan <ben.horgan@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Catalin Marinas <catalin.marinas@arm.com>

Here is the root cause:
The function __destroy_component_cfg() could be called before the configuration array (comp->cfg) is allocated, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when it attempts to add comp->cfg to the garbage list via add_to_garbage().

Here is the patch:
 
 static void __destroy_component_cfg(struct mpam_component *comp)
 {
 	struct mpam_msc *msc;
 	struct mpam_vmsc *vmsc;
 	struct mpam_msc_ris *ris;
 
 	lockdep_assert_held(&mpam_list_lock);
 
+	if (!comp->cfg)
+		return;
+
 	add_to_garbage(comp->cfg);
 	list_for_each_entry(vmsc, &comp->vmsc, comp_list) {
 		msc = vmsc->msc;
 
 		if (mpam_mon_sel_lock(msc)) {
 			list_for_each_entry(ris, &vmsc->ris, vmsc_list)
 				add_to_garbage(ris->mbwu_state);
 			mpam_mon_sel_unlock(msc);
 		}
 	}
 }
